articles.title: Malachi Toney Reacts to Historic Record-Setting Performance in Miami's Win vs. Stanford
articles.summary: Malachi Toney said setting Miami's new single-game receiving yards record was made more meaningful by the caliber of wideouts on the program's leaderboard.
articles.body:
Malachi Toney said setting Miami's new single-game receiving yards record was made more meaningful by the caliber of wideouts on the program's leaderboard.

Toney racked up 234 receiving yards in Friday's season-opening win over Stanford to beat the single-game program record set 42 years ago by Eddie Brown.

"It means a lot knowing how many greats played at this university," Toney told reporters after Miami's 45-6 victory. "Just for me to be the player to break that record and set a new one, it just means a lot."

Toney started out Friday's game with a 48-yard reception and went on to make three touchdown catches, including a 47-yard score in the third quarter.

His performance helped quarterback Darian Mensah finish the game having missed just three of 30 pass attempts while throwing for 401 yards.

Multiple legendary Miami wide receivers were watching Toney open the season with a historic performance.

WPLG Local 10's Will Manso shared a video of former Hurricanes and Dallas Cowboys star Michael Irvin congratulating Toney after the win.

Former Miami standout and current Indianapolis Colts wide receivers coach Reggie Wayne also shouted out Toney's performance on social media.

Toney led the nation with 109 catches and paced the ACC with 1,211 receiving yards during his true freshman 2025 season despite reclassifying to enroll in college early.

The wide receiver could establish himself as a Heisman Trophy candidate if he is able to continue building on his chemistry with Mensah in his age-19 season.

articles.title: Lane Kiffin's Dae'Quan Wright, Zxavian Harris LSU Roster Decision Revealed Ahead of Clemson Game
articles.summary: LSU didn't add tight end Dae'Quan Wright and defensive lineman Zxavian Harris to the team's roster for a season-opening clash with Clemson on Saturday, according to ESPN's Pete Thamel.
articles.body:
LSU didn't add tight end Dae'Quan Wright and defensive lineman Zxavian Harris to the team's roster for a season-opening clash with Clemson on Saturday, according to ESPN's Pete Thamel .

Thamel noted that both players could potentially be added later in the year, as they're enrolled at the school.

Report: Clemson Warns LSU of Contract Breach

On Thursday, a Louisiana judge issued a preliminary injunction against the NCAA in their eligibility case that paved the way for players such as Wright and Harris to suit up in college for a fifth year after spending time in NFL training camps.

However, Yahoo Sports' Ross Dellenger reported that Clemson general counsel Chip Hood sent a brief email to LSU's general counsel in which he brought up "certain eligibility" issues that may break "contractual obligations between the two parties."

The SEC and ACC were among several conferences that recently implemented rules to prevent players that previously declared for the NFL draft and did not withdraw consistent with NCAA requirements or signed a contract with an NFL team or another professional league from returning to play in college.

Wright reached an agreement with LSU for the 2026 season after clearing waivers upon his exit from the Cleveland Browns, while Harris committed to the Tigers after he was waived by the New Orleans Saints.

Although the SEC filed a lawsuit against LSU with a U.S. District Court in Alabama on Thursday alleging that the school violated the league's "First Amendment right of expressive association" by ignoring the new rules that prohibit the addition of former NFL players, the preliminary injunction still allowed Wright and Harris to play.

They won't be on the field when LSU and Clemson face off on Saturday at 7:30 p.m. ET, though.

articles.title: THE IMPOSSIBLE: Messi and Ronaldo could finally play together on same team after special invite from former teammate
articles.summary: Football News: Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo may finally play together in a historic farewell match organized by Carlos Tevez at Boca Juniors' La Bombonera. Tevez aims to gather football legends for a spectacular event, hoping to unite the iconic rivals on the same team. Stay tuned for this unprecedented moment in football history!
articles.body: Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo have spent almost two decades on opposite sides of football's biggest rivalry. They have faced each other 37 times, collected 13 Ballon d'Ors between them and spent years being measured against one another.Now, there is a chance the two could finally share a team.Messi and Ronaldo have both been invited to take part in Carlos Tevez's farewell match, with the former Argentina and Manchester United striker planning a spectacular gathering of his old teammates and friends at Boca Juniors' iconic La Bombonera later this year.Tevez wants Messi and Ronaldo on the same teamTevez retired in 2021 after his third spell with Boca, the club where he began his career, but five years on he is preparing one final celebration of his football life.According to TyC Sports' Marcelo Palacios, Tevez approached his former teammate Juan Román Riquelme, now Boca's president, about staging the game at La Bombonera. Riquelme has given the plan the green light, with officials now working on a date in December that does not clash with Boca's schedule.And Tevez has made no secret of the biggest names he wants involved.Around 60 star players are expected to attend the match, with Messi and Ronaldo naturally among the most sought-after guests.Tevez played alongside Messi for Argentina and spent three seasons with Ronaldo at Manchester United, with both players leaving Old Trafford in the same summer.The Argentine has remained in contact with both superstars and believes he can persuade them to take part.In an interview on streaming platform Olga, Tevez was asked whether Messi and Ronaldo could end up on opposite sides.“We'll get them together,” he replied.Tevez also said he still speaks to both players on WhatsApp. When asked how he planned to persuade Ronaldo to make the trip, his answer was characteristically direct:“I'll go get him myself.”It would be an extraordinary sight at La Bombonera if he succeeds.Messi, now with Inter Miami, and Ronaldo, still playing for Al Nassr, have spent their careers being compared rather than combined. Their rivalry defined an era of football, particularly during their years at Barcelona and Real Madrid, but the two have never played alongside one another at club or international level. Messi, however, officially closed the door on his international career, announcing on August 31, 2026, that he has immediately retired from the Argentina national team following their 1–0 defeat to Spain in the 2026 World Cup final. That makes the possibility of a shared appearance with Ronaldo, even in a testimonial, feel more significant.Tevez is now attempting to change that for one night.And his guest list does not stop there.Tevez has an extraordinary guest list in mindThe 41-year-old has already discussed a starting XI packed with players from different chapters of his career.For the goalkeepers, he wants two of the game's most decorated names: Edwin van der Sar and Gianluigi Buffon.At centre-back, his proposed group includes former Manchester United teammates Rio Ferdinand and Nemanja Vidic, alongside Italian defenders Giorgio Chiellini and Leonardo Bonucci.Tevez also has a place reserved for Patrice Evra, whom he affectionately described as his “brother”.“(Edwin) Van der Sar on one side and (Gianluigi) Buffon on the other,” Tevez said.“At centre back, we’ll probably have Rio Ferdinand, (Nemanja) Vidic… we’ll bring in (Giorgio) Chiellini, (Leonardo) Bonucci. Patrice Evra, my brother, he has to be there.”The midfield would be no less familiar to football fans, with Andrea Pirlo, Paul Scholes and Riquelme among those Tevez hopes to bring together.“Midfielders… (Andrea) Pirlo, Paul Scholes, Roman (Riquelme) will definitely be there. Rooney.”That list includes teammates from Tevez's time in England, Italy and Argentina, as well as some of the greatest opponents he encountered during his career.But even among a collection of Champions League winners, World Cup winners and international legends, there would be one sight that towers above the rest.Messi and Ronaldo standing on the same side of the pitch.It remains dependent on their availability, and neither has been confirmed for the game. But Tevez has already been clear about what he wants.After years of football history being written with Messi and Ronaldo separated by shirts, countries and rival clubs, the man who shared a dressing room with both is hoping to put them in the same one at La Bombonera — even if only for an afternoon.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Newcastle v Bournemouth: How the players rated
articles.summary: How Newcastle United and Bournemouth's players rated in their Premier League match.
articles.body:
Substitute Jacob Ramsey scored a late equaliser as Newcastle United came from behind to draw 2-2 against Bournemouth at St James' Park.

Here's how I rated the players and you can see how you scored them below.

What do BBC Sport's player ratings mean?

Late Ramsey equaliser earns point for Newcastle against Bournemouth

Lukas Hornicek: A little unfortunate for the second goal in particular after the ball came back off the upright and bounced off him. One or two moments of miscommunication at the back. 5

Amar Dedic: Made an impressive start to his Newcastle career, and carries a real threat going forward, but caught out defensively for both goals. Did swing in the ball for the equaliser, though. 4

Malick Thiaw: Stand-in captain in Dan Burn's absence once again, but could only watch on as he put through the net after his block on Alex Scott's cross looped into the bottom corner. 5

Sven Botman: A poor clearance before Marcus Tavernier's opener but went on to make a couple of crucial interventions to deny Evanilson. 5

Lewis Hall: Substituted at half-time in the corresponding fixture back in April but coped better with Rayan this time. 6

Nico Gonzalez: Struggled to have the same effect as his impressive debut against Tottenham Hotspur . Missed a tackle on Tavernier before Bournemouth 's second goal and only partially blocked Scott's effort in the build-up to the visitors' first . 5

Lewis Miley: So much potential, and still so young at 20, but struggled to get a handle on Bournemouth 's midfield. Passing not to usual standard. 5

Anthony Elanga: Quickly frustrated with refereeing decisions going against him. Got little change from Adrien Truffert. 5

Joe Willock: Couldn't fault his effort as he chased down Bournemouth players and attempted to make blocks. Came close to equalising with a header. 5

Harvey Barnes: Stepped up when Newcastle were on very shaky ground with a stunning goal from the hosts' first shot on target. Often frustrated by failure, but always capable of a big moment. 7

Yoane Wissa: Looks better in the number 10 role in this system than up top. Repeatedly dropped deep to get involved. Showed determination to dig out a cross for a big Willock chance. 5

Matias Fernandez-Pardo (on 63, Willock): Got a huge welcome on his debut. Quickly won a free-kick and worked hard to win the ball back. 6

Jacob Ramsey: Popped up with a precious equaliser to secure a point with a well-taken finish. 7

Subs not used: Nick Pope, Fabian Schar, Aladji Bamba, Bazoumana Toure

Djordje Petrovic : Little he could do for Barnes' goal, but otherwise a relatively comfortable afternoon. 6

Adam Smith: Played a role in Tavernier's opener by nudging the ball to Scott in the build-up. Tested on one or two moments defensively, but still showing his value at 35 . 6

James Hill: Solid. Has already become a very important player for manager Marco Rose. 6

Antonio Silva: Took a nasty blow to the head from Elanga's shoulder, but the summer signing shook it off. 6

Adrien Truffert: Coped expertly with the in-form Elanga and caused Dedic real problems going the other way. 7

Tyler Adams: First competitive start under Rose. Could have got closer to Barnes for Newcastle 's goal, but hard to see him coming out of the side after this display. 7

Alex Scott: So influential. Played a key role in both of his side's goals. Passing and vision stood out throughout. 8

Rayan: Not as effective as he was in the corresponding fixture last season. Rose was roaring at him at one stage. 5

Marcus Tavernier: Showed great anticipation to put the visitors in front. He's now scored in each of his past three trips to St James' Park. Could have netted a couple on this visit . 7

Justin Kluivert: Helped set up Bournemouth 's crucial second goal after boldly letting fly from 35 yards out. Always a handful. 7

Evanilson: Had a real battle with Botman. Missed a couple of decent chances but worked hard throughout. 6

Subs not used: Michele Di Gregorio, Julio Soler, Bafode Diakite, Juanlu Sanchez

articles.title: Luka Modric: Croatia midfielder to continue international career
articles.summary: Luke Modric, 41, is not ready to retire from international football and hopes to play for Croatia in upcoming Nations League games, including against England.
articles.body:
Luka Modric turns 41 on Wednesday but is not ready to retire from international football just yet.

The Croatia FA has announced , external that their captain intends to continue playing for the national team in upcoming Nations League games, including against England.

His decision coincides with the return of Slaven Bilic as manager , with the former West Ham boss helping to guide Modric's fledgling international career in his first stint in charge of the Croatia side, between 2006 and 2012.

Modric earned his first senior cap in March 2006, just before Bilic was named Croatia manager for the first time, and has since gone on to make 202 appearances for his country.

He was expected to call it a day after this summer's World Cup, when Zlatko Dalic's side were knocked out in the last 32 by Portugal.

"Of course, Luka's decision makes me extremely happy," said Bilic, who was manager of Croatia when they denied Steve McLaren's England side qualification for the 2008 Euros.

"We are all aware what he brings to Croatia, both on and off the pitch.

"I'm looking forward to working with him again, after 14 years, and we both share a strong ambition to keep Croatia a top, successful team, shoulder to shoulder with the best teams in the world."

Modric, who currently plays for AC Milan, won the Golden Ball at the 2018 World Cup in Russia, when he helped Croatia reach the final, where they lost to France.

He was also part of the side that finished third in Qatar, four years later.

After playing his part in McLaren's "wally with the brolly" moment at Wembley in the 2008 Euro qualifiers, Modric helped Croatia reach the quarter-finals in Austria and Switzerland.

Croatia's next internationals are in the in the Nations League - away to Czech Republic on 26 September and Spain on 29 September.

They then host England in the competition on 3 October, with the return fixture at Wembley on 12 November.

articles.title: Coach Luis Enrique unconcerned by PSG’s poor start to French league season
articles.summary: Two points from three matches is ⁠their worst start since the 2007-08 season, when PSG came close to relegation.
articles.body:
Paris Saint-Germain ‌have not had as poor a start to a league season ⁠for 19 years, ⁠with Friday’s home loss to Monaco leaving them winless after three matches in the Ligue 1 season.

Days before they begin the defence ⁠of their Champions League title, however, the Parisians have handed coach Luis Enrique a contract extension until 2030.

“There is no reason to be concerned. I ⁠say that honestly. How many shots on target did Monaco have? Two. How many goals? Two. We’ll see at the end of the season whether things balance out,” he said after Friday’s 2-1 setback in which they were ahead at halftime ‌but conceded twice after the break.

“What I want to get across is that you shouldn’t look only at the result,” Luis Enrique added.

“We pressed sensationally, much better than in many matches when we did not concede a goal. But luck was not on our side.

“Monaco know that if they play against us like this 10 times, we win eight, there’d be one ⁠draw and we’d lose once. This was that one ⁠defeat,” Luis Enrique insisted as PSG look ahead to hosting Slovan Bratislava on Wednesday in their first Champions League group game, chasing a third successive European title.

Two points from three matches is ⁠their worst start since the 2007-08 season, when PSG came close to relegation, finishing 16th. In that campaign, Paul ⁠Le Guen’s side had to wait until their ⁠sixth league game to record a victory and ended up only three points above the relegation places.

This time round, the Parisians are already seven points off the pace.

“It is incredible motivation for my ‌players, for the team and for the club. If you want to bet on who will be champions at the end of the season, we can ‌place ‌a bet. Seven points? OK, we will try to make up that deficit as quickly as possible,” the coach added.

articles.title: Jayden Daniels Trolled by Young Fan With 'College GameDay' Sign After No. 5 LSU Jersey Saga
articles.summary: If Jayden Daniels thought the mockery toward him had dissipated, the former LSU star was sorely mistaken Saturday morning.
articles.body:
If Jayden Daniels thought the mockery toward him had dissipated, the former LSU star was sorely mistaken Saturday morning.

One young fan in a No. 5 jersey held a sign during College GameDay that read, "Jayden. Don't sue me. I'm only 7."

Report: Clemson Warns LSU of Contract Breach

Daniels left Baton Rouge with a lot of goodwill thanks to winning the 2023 Heisman Trophy. However, he brought himself some scorn when he sent LSU a cease and desist letter for the use of his name, image and likeness.

The Washington Commanders quarterback was upset coach Lane Kiffin allowed cornerback DJ Pickett to wear No. 5 this year.

Any search on social media for the phrase "out of respect for Jayden Daniels" will yield a lot of jokes at his expense:

A little more consequentially, a portion of the Tigers fanbase turned on Daniels.

One long-standing axiom in sports is that no one player is bigger than the team. That applies particularly to college athletics, where athletes come and go so frequently.

In the case of Daniels, he won a Heisman but was only in Baton Rouge for two years. And during that time, LSU combined to go 20-7 and miss the College Football Playoff. The 2022 and 2023 seasons weren't that memorable in the grand scheme of things.

Daniels didn't do enough to warrant the kind of status he was expecting in the eyes of some fans. Joe Burrow likewise was on campus for just two years but played a starring role on what was one of the greatest college teams in modern history.

In time, a lot of this will probably be forgotten, and the No. 5 jersey could eventually be retired in Daniels' honor. For now, he'd be advised to steer clear of Louisiana.

articles.title: Chelsea 1-1 Aston Villa: Lauren James strike cancelled out late on as Villa earn historic point at Stamford Bridge

articles.body:
Lauren James had given Chelsea a deserved lead after just 11 minutes, capitalising on a mistake in the Villa defence before shifting the ball onto her left foot and firing powerfully into the roof of the net.

Chelsea remained on top and Aggie Beever-Jones, making her 100th appearance for the club, was denied by Akane Okuma before Sjoeke Nusken fired over as the hosts went into the break with a slender advantage.

Villa improved after half-time and Amalie Vangsgaard passed up a huge opportunity to equalise when she met Chasity Grant's cross at the near post but fired narrowly wide. Chelsea then went within inches of doubling their advantage as Keira Walsh's long-range effort crashed against the underside of the crossbar.

The visitors made Chelsea pay in the 79th minute. A mix-up inside the home penalty area allowed Noelle Maritz to react quickest and her close-range effort deflected off Veerle Buurman and into the net for an own goal.

Chelsea pushed for a winner and almost found one in the final minute of normal time, but Okuma produced a superb reaction save to somehow turn James' close-range effort over the crossbar and preserve a point for Villa.

The result means Chelsea begin their attempt to reclaim the WSL title with a draw in their first league game since making Stamford Bridge their permanent home, while Villa end a run of 12 successive league defeats against the Blues to make an encouraging start to their campaign.

articles.title: Newcastle 2-2 Bournemouth: Jacob Ramsey scores late equaliser as Cherries blow another lead
articles.summary: Report as Newcastle fight back to draw 2-2 with Bournemouth; Marcus Tavernier scored and Malick Thiaw netted own goal to give Cherries two-goal lead; Harvey Barnes and Jacob Ramsey hauled Newcastle level; Bournemouth have lost seven points from winning positions this season
articles.body:
Bournemouth appeared on track for their first win under Marco Rose after an early strike from Marcus Tavernier and a Malick Thiaw own goal, only to blow a late lead for the third straight game.

Harvey Barnes halved the deficit with a stunning curler 27 seconds after the kick-off following Bournemouth's second goal, before substitute Ramsey found the bottom corner in the 88th minute to continue Newcastle's unbeaten start under Matthias Jaissle.

Bournemouth were the better side overall, attempting 17 shots compared to only eight from the lacklustre hosts, but Ramsey's leveller follows crucial stoppage-time goals conceded in their games against Manchester City and Everton.

Latest news and rumours: Newcastle | Bournemouth

The Cherries have lost seven points from winning positions this term. They are the first side in Premier League history to score the opening goal in their first three games and fail to win any of them.

9: GOAL! Tavernier is alert to bury the loose ball after Scott's effort is deflected

35: GOAL! Thiaw turns Scott's cross into his own net after Kluivert's shot hit the post

37: GOAL! Barnes cuts inside from the left before curling home a brilliant strike

52: CHANCE! A flicked header from Willock bounces inches wide for Newcastle

63: WELCOME! Matias Fernandez-Pardo gets a warm reception as he appears for his Newcastle debut

88: GOAL! Ramsey strokes a composed finish into the bottom corner to equalise

Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle to TNT Sports : "Mixed feelings.

"Happy for that spirit, that belief the lads were showing until the end together with the crowd. I felt the energy and felt if we had five or 10 minutes more we could win this game.

"But the first half was not expected. This is something we need to improve. This is part of the journey.

"We knew Bournemouth would come with everything; they always show great intensity and if you do not compete with that you get problems.

"We struggled with that in the first half but the lads showed the right reaction."

Bournemouth boss Marco Rose to TNT Sports : "It is what it is.

"I'm really happy with the confidence the lads brought on the pitch today. Especially in the first half, we were so good. We could have scored even a third goal.

"Then more or less from nothing we conceded a really nice goal to Newcastle, then the game is open here in this stadium. Second half we missed the chances, the transition situations, possession... In the end it's a draw and we have to deal with it.

"It's good that we're in situations to be able to win games. The other things we have to talk about, we have to finish games, we need to defend our own goal like it's the last game in our life.

"If you always concede one or two, you need to score three to win and that's pretty hard in the Premier League."

Ramsey's goal ensured Newcastle remain unbeaten under Eddie Howe's successor, but they might count themselves a little fortunate on this occasion. Bournemouth, by contrast, will wonder how they didn't win.

Jaissle has issues to address but Ramsey's impact showed his value to the side and there was also a positive debut from new £51m signing Matias Fernandez-Pardo, who emerged to warm applause when he came on as a second-half substitute.

The Belgian international is of course new to the Premier League. He was on the receiving end of a couple of meaty challenges to welcome him. But there were glimpses of his talent, too, including a clever drop of the shoulder to escape pressure in the box. He injected some much-needed energy and directness.

It was 90+1 vs Man City. Then 90+1 vs Everton. And now 88 at Newcastle. Bournemouth's failure to see out the final minutes of matches has cost them dearly in their first three games.

The late goals must be infuriating for Rose, whose side would have been sitting top of the table going into Saturday's 3pm games had they held out in the final minutes of their matches so far.

It will be a particularly galling journey back to the south coast from Newcastle, given how Bournemouth dominated the first half and missed two good chances to add to their tally before the break, with Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson off target.

Rose will also reflect on how his side seemingly allowed the game to fizzle out in that second half before Newcastle's smash-and-grab. Fine margins. Had they held on, it would have looked like a perfect away performance.

But Bournemouth's lack of intensity and focus in the final minutes has seen them give up precious points again.

articles.title: Stoke City 4-0 Charlton Athletic: Potters romp to comfortable win
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Stoke City and Charlton Athletic at the bet365 Stadium on Saturday; Justin Devenny's double double, Ethan Galbraith and George Hirst seal an emphatic win for the Potters.
articles.body:
The Addicks had not lost a league game this season before their visit to the bet365 Stadium, but a brilliant brace from debutant Justin Devenny and other first-half goals from Ethan Galbraith and George Hirst saw the Potters put the contest to bed before the break.

Second-half substitute Danny McNamara was sent off for two careless yellow cards in the space of three minutes as the afternoon spiralled spectacularly out of control for the visitors.

Booked first for pulling back Eric Bocat, full-back McNamara was dismissed in the 50th minute after berating referee Robert Madley.

Stoke should have gone on to score more goals, but the second half was a stroll as both sides played possession football with the result all but confirmed.

Charlton had started the brighter of the two sides and could have easily been ahead after some good early pressure.

Former Stoke striker Tyreece Campbell had a goalbound shot charged down in the eighth minute and then skipper Lloyd Jones shot wide from close-range.

However, it was one-way traffic after that.

Galbraith cut inside and saw his powerful left-foot curler deflected over as Stoke countered, before the hosts took the lead from the penalty spot in the 15th minute.

Charlton debutant Timothy Ouma, one of four changes for the visitors, was adjudged to have bundled over Ben Wilmot in the box and new signing Devenny coolly slotted into the bottom left corner for his first goal since joining from Crystal Palace.

Hirst headed over from a Galbraith cross soon after before the latter doubled Stoke's lead with a fine finish into the bottom left corner in the 22nd minute.

The jubilant Stoke fans could not resist teasing their former manager with the chant "cheer up Nathan Jones" as the afternoon started to unravel for the visitors.

Three minutes later it was 3-0 when Hirst headed home from close-range from a delightful Bocat cross from the left.

Northern Ireland international Devenney fired wide of the right post on the half hour mark and Bosun Lawal headed over as Stoke dominated.

And they got a fourth four minutes before half-time when the impressive Devenny rifled into the bottom right corner to leave the Addicks with a mountain to climb.

McNamara was sent off five minutes after the restart to compound a poor trip for the Addicks who, after conceding so many in the first half, were never in the contest after that.

Replacement Jack McGlynn had a decent chance to make it 5-0 with eight minutes remaining but he struck his left-foot shot straight at goalkeeper Arthur Okonkwo.

Addicks sub Millenic Alli tried his luck with a long-range effort two minutes later, but his shot flew high and wide, summing up a bad day for the off-colour Londoners.

"If we could have written a [perfect] script, then that would have been it. I thought we played really well. There was a lot to be pleased about.

"On the back of the other night [a 1-0 home win over Norwich] it was really important we had a really good performance against a side that was unbeaten before the game. And we certainly got that.

"We created some momentum with our play and, I've got to say, all four of the goals were fantastic.

"We've got the penalty and then we've scored some good goals. "Shooting has been really lacking for a long time, but they did that well today.

"When you look at what we have, then you're looking for goals. We've got players that are really hungry for that.

"If we can get that throughout the team, well, then that really bodes well, because I'd like to see us scoring more from set-plays as well."

"I've gone in and seen him [the referee]. I'm bitterly disappointed with my own team's performance, but I'm as bitterly disappointed with another performance as well.

"There were so many things that went against us but straight after the penalty we went under for 20 minutes - and my teams don't normally do that.

"But we've done it twice here. That's the thing that hurts me and hurts my teams, us going under like that.

"I think they [Stoke] need me to come here because they get better results when I get back.

"We had a great start and wanted to silence the crowd, but we gave away an absolute gift [for the opening goal]. That can't happen.

"But after the penalty, fair play to Stoke, they never looked back. After that gift of the penalty they were far better.

"I'm definitely going to get it [a hostile reception] when I come back here, but I expected that. I had it when I was manager, so I'm definitely going to get it as an opposing manager."

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Preston North End 2-1 Blackburn Rovers: Callum Lang double seals win for Lilywhites
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Preston North End and Blackburn Rovers at Deepdale on Saturday; Callum Lang scores twice as Lilywhites pick up their first points of the season in Lancashire derby.
articles.body:
The 27-year-old opened the scoring with a poacher's finish in the ninth minute before nodding in a 28th-minute second.

Stanley Mills accidentally halved the arrears early in the second half with an unfortunate own goal on just his second Preston start but his team held on for their first win of the season.

Preston fell behind early on in their last match with Bristol City and Daniel Iversen had to make vital saves twice in the opening five minutes here, first backpedalling to claw Yuri Ribeiro's looping corner off the line and then standing tall to block Todd Cantwell one-on-one after the former Norwich man latched onto Adam Forshaw's deflected pass.

After those initial scares, North End supporters were up off their seats in jubilation as Lang ghosted in at the back post to fire Delano Burgzorg's excellent drilled delivery across Aynsley Pears and into the corner.

Tony Mowbray would have been left scratching his head at how his men were behind and Blackburn continued to probe with Ryoya Morishita having their best opening on 23 minutes, linking up well with Andri Gudjohnsen before seeing his shot from the centre of the box flash over the bar via a slight deflection.

Incredibly, the visitors went two behind in the simplest of ways as Lang connected with Jordan Thompson's inswinging free-kick before Pears, nicking it past the 28-year-old stopper to double North End's advantage.

Leo Leroy wasted a golden chance to get Preston's third with a poorly weighted through-ball to Burgzorg as Blackburn's defence were on the ropes and, at the other end, Morishita skied well over after more good link-up with Gudjohnsen.

Blackburn started the second half the same as the first, on the front foot, only this time they got their just deserts in the 51st minute as Ryan Alebiosu's cross took a nick off Lewis Gibson and team-mate Mills turned it into his own net under pressure from Dapo Afolayan.

Preston could have restored their two-goal cushion on the hour as Leroy found Burgzorg with just Pears to beat but the goalkeeper got a glove on the Suriname striker's shot.

Jayden Fevrier came on for the visitors and on 66 minutes, two minutes after his introduction, rattled the bar with an audacious effort from the corner of the box.

The basketball-like nature of the game continued in the 72nd minute as Kristi Montgomery blocked bravely from Alfie Devine with the attacker's low shot from Harry Clarke's centre destined for the corner.

Iversen had to turn Cantwell's swivelling shot to safety before making a similar stop to deny Fevrier shortly afterwards, but Preston held on to the spoils.

"[Lang's] worked really hard in the closed season. He was training all summer, but he's still been careful, sensible within the pre-season and the start of the season with his schedule.

"We want to build up that resilience in his body, definitely. But more importantly, when he's playing, we want to make sure he can go flat out like he did today.

"Lang [attacks] the ball really well in the box and I think his two goals are a good example of that.

"Two really good goals [from] Lang's point of view and [that's] where we wanted him and the deliveries in the box [were good]. But for me, the best thing about us today is that spirit and the determination to see the game out."

"I think if you fall below the standard you set yourself, then you shouldn't really expect that you're going to win. We came here believing we were going to win and we conceded two really soft goals, which is so unlike us.

"We went to Lincoln just three days ago and it felt like you chased a thousand crosses and we headed them all out. We never really got to the level we needed to to get our second goal.

"At the end of the day, and I don't think I'm talking out of turn, I think we were ultimately on top for most of the game, possession-wise, pace, field-tilt they call it these days. [Preston's half] is probably where the game was played mostly.
